 Luka Dončić went off in Friday’s win over the Trail Blazers, finishing with 53 points (17-of-33 FGs, 14-of-18 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
 Dončić finished Friday’s victory with his 11th 50-point game, moving past Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Allen Iverson to land in tenth on the league’s all-time list. But that wasn’t the only history the Lakers star made on Friday. Dončić has tallied at least 35 points, five rebounds, and five assists in seven straight games, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in league history. Also, Dončić, who outscored Portland 20-15 in the third quarter, has scored at least 40 points in four straight games. He’s on an incredible run, which is great for those rostering Dončić.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Luka Dončić had himself a night with 40 points (11-of-23 FGs, 12-of-13 FTs), nine rebounds, seven assists, a steal, a block, six 3-pointers, and six turnovers in 116-103 win over the Kings. 
 Luka’s MVP campaign continues in Sacramento where he puts another massive statement game against the Kings. He took over in the third quarter, and the Lakers separated themselves against the Kings in this game. He’s been everything you could’ve wanted and more this season and the hope is that he doesn’t get hurt.

 Luka Dončić led the Lakers with 42 points (14-of-24 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), seven rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and six three-pointers in a 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday. 
 It has been an unreal start to the season for Dončić, and Monday’s performance was just another chapter. He has scored at least 35 points and knocked down at least six three-pointers in each of his last five appearances, while going for at least 40 in four of those outings. The one game he didn’t score 40, he had 37, which was also the only game during this stretch where he shot below 50 percent from the floor. Dončić set a new season high for assists in this game as well. He has been an elite offensive engine, and he’ll look to stay hot against the Kings on Wednesday.

 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Raptors with 45 points (12-of-23 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show Sunday night, shooting high percentages from the field and the foul line as part of an elite stat line. With the Lakers’ deep reserves failing to put the Raptors away, head coach JJ Redick had to insert four starters back into the game. That got Dončić four more points from the foul line. The lone negative was the seven turnovers, but the stat line was so robust that few will complain. The Lakers play four games next week, starting with the Heat on Monday.

 Luka Dončić accumulated 37 points (12-of-27 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal, two blocks and six three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Warriors. 
 Dončić was rolling during the first quarter, knocking down five three-pointers and scoring 21 points. Unfortunately for the Lakers, their star guard needed a rest to start the second quarter, which opened the door for the Warriors to turn things around. While Dončić scored 13 second-half points, he didn’t get enough help from teammates beyond Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler to avoid the defeat. The Lakers host Toronto on Sunday to end their week.

 Luka Dončić amassed 41 points (12-of-22 FGs, 11-of-13 Fts), five rebounds, nine assists, one block and six three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 One game removed from dropping 52 points on the Jazz, Dončić had another prolific scoring night on Tuesday. In addition to the high field-goal percentage, he kept the turnovers in check, committing only two. Despite averaging nearly six turnovers per game, Dončić has been one of the most valuable players in nine-cat formats. Shooting 87.5 percent from the foul line, which represents significant improvement, certainly helps.

 Luka Dončić finished Sunday’s win over the Jazz with 52 points (17-of-30 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, two steals and eight three-pointers. 
 Dončić put on a show in Salt Lake City, recording his first 50-point game of the new season. And he was highly efficient, shooting well over 50 percent from the field. The only thing that could have made Sunday better for managers rostering Dončić was getting the two rebounds he needed to finish with a triple-double. The Lakers play four games in Week 2, starting Tuesday against the Trail Blazers.

 Luka Dončić tallied 23 points (8-of-21 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers. 
 After an excellent start to his 2026-27 season against the Warriors on Wednesday, Dončić had some efficiency issues on Friday. While category league managers won’t be too concerned with the percentages, the Lakers’ point guard racked up a career-high 11 turnovers. By now, many managers rostering Dončić are fine with punting that category, but it’s still a startling number for him. He’ll look to put together a better showing when the Lakers visit the Jazz on Sunday.

 Lillard led the team in points on Friday, but the production was lacking outside of points and three-pointers.  Reaves struggled to begin Friday’s game, missing his first seven shots. However, he shone in the second and fourth quarters, shooting 7-of-12 from the field and scoring 23 of his 25 points. Even with Friday’s poor shooting, Reaves is shooting nearly 51 percent from the field.  Victor Wembanyama had himself a night with 30 points (10-of-18 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), 14 rebounds, two assists, two blocks, and four 3-pointers in the 124-109 win over the Kings. 
 Wembanyama just took advantage of the Kings defense and got whatever he wanted. What is notable is that he did role his ankle near the end of the first half due to a Sabonis closeout, so it’s possible he shows up on the injury report, but he did finish the game which is good to see. Compared to his stat line last game, this performance seems like a letdown which goes to show how good Wembanyama is.

 Acuff didn’t have much of an issue scoring against this Kings defense. His ability as a rookie to take on usage, be relatively efficient, and get buckets and run the offense is impressive.
